slides.title: Meiosis and fertilization together maintain chromosome-set balance
text: Meiosis and fertilization together maintain chromosome-set balance
Meiosis and fertilization together maintain chromosome-set balance.
Meiosis halves the chromosome sets in gametes. Fertilization brings two sets together again, maintaining chromosome number while allowing genetic variety.

slides.title: Chromosomes carry genes at defined positions called loci
text: Chromosomes carry genes at defined positions called loci
Chromosomes carry genes at defined positions called loci.
Genes are DNA segments carried on chromosomes. Their location is called a locus, and gametes pass this genetic information to offspring.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q1: What term is given to the specific, defined position that a gene occupies on a chromosome?
Locus
Centriole
Nucleolus
Ribosome

slides.title: Sexual reproduction recombines genetic information from gametes
text: Sexual reproduction recombines genetic information from gametes
Sexual reproduction recombines genetic information from gametes.
Asexual reproduction usually produces clones from one parent. Sexual reproduction combines gametes, producing new combinations of inherited genes.

slides.title: Homologs are parental counterparts; sisters are replication copies
text: Homologs are parental counterparts; sisters are replication copies
Homologs are parental counterparts; sisters are replication copies.
Homologs come from different parents and carry corresponding gene positions. Sister chromatids are the replicated copies of one chromosome.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q2: Where do the two members of a pair of homologous chromosomes typically originate from in a diploid organism?
Both chromosomes come from the mother during gamete formation
One chromosome comes from the mother and the other from the father
Both chromosomes are synthesized via independent DNA replication in the zygote
One chromosome is inherited entirely from asexual budding while the other is lost

slides.title: Diploid and haploid describe chromosome sets, not DNA quantity
text: Diploid and haploid describe chromosome sets, not DNA quantity
Diploid and haploid describe chromosome sets, not DNA quantity.
Typical human body cells have 46 chromosomes in two sets. Gametes have 23 in one set, and DNA replication does not change set number.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q3: A standard human sperm cell contains (n = 23) chromosomes. How are these 23 chromosomes specifically categorized?
22 autosomes and 1 sex chromosome
23 autosomes and 0 sex chromosomes
21 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes
44 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes

slides.title: Meiosis reduces sets, fertilization restores them, and mitosis supports growth
text: Meiosis reduces sets, fertilization restores them, and mitosis supports growth
Meiosis reduces sets, fertilization restores them, and mitosis supports growth.
The human cycle alternates diploid adults and haploid gametes. Fertilization restores diploidy, and mitosis supports growth without changing chromosome-set number.

slides.title: The growing stage differs across sexual life-cycle patterns
text: The growing stage differs across sexual life-cycle patterns
The growing stage differs across sexual life-cycle patterns.
Sexual life cycles differ in which stages grow as multicellular organisms. Plants include haploid and diploid generations, while the animal example emphasizes diploid adults.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q4: In animals, what is the ploidy level of the multicellular adult stage, and what type of reproductive cells are produced directly by meiosis?
Haploid (n); spores
Diploid (2n); spores (n)
Diploid (2n); gametes (n)
Haploid (n); zygotes (2n)

slides.title: One replication supports two successive meiotic divisions
text: One replication supports two successive meiotic divisions
One replication supports two successive meiotic divisions.
Meiosis copies DNA once and divides twice. Homologs separate first, sisters separate second, producing four haploid cells in the general sequence.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q5: How many rounds of DNA replication occur in support of the two successive divisions of meiosis?
Two rounds, to prepare for both divisions separately
Three rounds, matching the final number of cell stages
One round, which supports both Meiosis I and Meiosis II
Zero rounds, as meiosis only involves division without replication

slides.title: Meiosis I separates homologs while sisters remain joined
text: Meiosis I separates homologs while sisters remain joined
Meiosis I separates homologs while sisters remain joined.
During meiosis I, homologs pair, line up and separate. Each resulting cell is haploid, but its chromosomes still contain joined sister chromatids.

slides.title: The second division separates sisters without another DNA replication
text: The second division separates sisters without another DNA replication
The second division separates sisters without another DNA replication.
Meiosis II separates the sister chromatids within each haploid cell. The general result is four haploid cells with unduplicated chromosomes.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q1: Does DNA replication occur immediately before Meiosis II begins?
Yes, complete DNA replication occurs to ensure all chromosomes are doubled
No, Meiosis II takes place without another round of DNA replication
Yes, but only for sex chromosomes
Only partial replication happens to reduce chromosome number

slides.title: Crossing over rearranges alleles within chromosomes
text: Crossing over rearranges alleles within chromosomes
Crossing over rearranges alleles within chromosomes.
Crossing over exchanges corresponding DNA between nonsister chromatids in prophase I. The recombinant products carry new combinations of maternal and paternal DNA.

slides.title: Mitosis preserves set number, while meiosis reduces it
text: Mitosis preserves set number, while meiosis reduces it
Mitosis preserves set number, while meiosis reduces it.
Mitosis produces two generally matching cells while preserving chromosome sets. Meiosis uses two divisions to produce four haploid products with genetic variation.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q2: What happens to the chromosome set number in a cell undergoing mitosis compared to one undergoing meiosis?
Mitosis halves the chromosome set number, while meiosis preserves it
Mitosis preserves the chromosome set number (diploid to diploid), while meiosis halves it (diploid to haploid)
Both mitosis and meiosis halve the chromosome set number
Both mitosis and meiosis preserve the chromosome set number.

slides.title: Independent assortment generates many combinations of whole chromosomes
text: Independent assortment generates many combinations of whole chromosomes
Independent assortment generates many combinations of whole chromosomes.
Each homologous pair orients independently. Two pairs allow four possible combinations, and 23 human pairs allow about 8.4 million before counting crossing over.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q3: What primary outcome is generated by the independent assortment of whole chromosomes during meiosis?
The exact replication of maternal chromosomes only
The permanent fusion of homologous chromosome pairs
A large variety of distinct whole-chromosome combinations in gametes
A reduction in the total number of chromosomes in somatic cells

slides.title: Random fertilization multiplies the assortment possibilities of two gametes
text: Random fertilization multiplies the assortment possibilities of two gametes
Random fertilization multiplies the assortment possibilities of two gametes.
Combining sperm and egg possibilities gives about 70 trillion possible human zygote combinations. That estimate still excludes the extra variation from crossing over.

slides.title: New alleles and new combinations play different roles in variation
text: New alleles and new combinations play different roles in variation
New alleles and new combinations play different roles in variation.
Mutation supplies new alleles, and sexual reproduction reshuffles them. The resulting heritable variation provides material on which natural selection can act.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q4: Why is heritable variation described as the "material" for natural selection?
Because natural selection requires phenotypic differences that can be passed down to offspring to favor certain variants
Because it prevents any future mutations from occurring in the population
Because it ensures every individual in the population is genetically identical
Because it completely replaces the need for sexual reproduction

slides.title: Stable chromosome number and genetic variety can occur together
text: Stable chromosome number and genetic variety can occur together
Stable chromosome number and genetic variety can occur together.
Meiosis and fertilization balance chromosome sets. Assortment, crossing over and random fertilization create variety, while mutation supplies new alleles.

slides.title: Thought Questions
text: Thought Questions
Q5: What is the primary change in chromosome ploidy level that occurs during the process of meiosis?
From haploid (n) to diploid (2n)
From diploid (2n) to haploid (n)
From diploid (2n) to tetraploid (4n)
From haploid (n) to haploid (n)
